notes: The parts are the same as in step 1. I added and dropped none.

Circuit text: pin 9 goes through the 100 ohm resistor to one speaker terminal, and the other terminal goes to GND. The photoresistor is powered from 5V. Its other end goes to A0, and the 4.7K resistor runs from that node to GND.

The page gives no breadboard hole positions, so I chose columns that keep each net separate. Nets: pin 9 = column 10; the 100 ohm resistor and speaker lead 1 = column 14; speaker lead 2 and the GND wire = column 18; 5V and the photoresistor = column 22; A0, the photoresistor and the 4.7K resistor = column 24; the 4.7K resistor and its GND wire = column 26. All of these are in the top bank, rows a to c.
I used the speaker's leads as breadboard connections, so spk1 ports 1 and 2 go into the breadboard. The speaker is symmetric, so either orientation works.
The GND wires use Uno GND.1 (digital header, as the image shows for the speaker side) and GND.2 (power header, for the 4.7K resistor).
Every physical connection has a joined edge and an electrical edge on the same ports.
The schematic image did not load, so the connections come from the circuit text and the breadboard image.
